correctness.rationale: The proof fixes the hub by complement symmetry, derives each rebel rim best reply directly from the three-neighbor majority, identifies all-rebel rim zero positions as maximal independent sets of C_n, proves Perrin enumeration via a three-state transfer matrix with characteristic polynomial λ³−λ−1, and checks the hub parity/strictness. In the one-defect case the conformist must play opposite to the hub, forces neighbor bits 1 and next-neighbor bits 0, and gives a bijection to ordered 2/3 compositions of n−4 with a length-four boundary gap; this gap ensures the hub rebel is strictly satisfied and hub conformist cannot best respond. n=3 and n=4 overlap cases are explicitly treated. Direct enumeration of all 524224 action profiles in 52 cases n=3..15 matches both total and strict counts; finite tests only support, not establish, the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact infinite-family four-case phase table treats an established binary network equilibrium model on a natural minimal nonbipartite wheel graph, with exact multiplicities, strictness and a sharp local-type perturbation. A single converted rim player extinguishes all conformist-hub equilibria for every even n, while a rebel hub has only strict equilibria whenever its composition count is positive. This is a structural robustness comparison, not an arbitrary numeric slice or a restatement of the known Perrin cycle identity. No downstream theorem or dynamics is asserted.
